run.question:
The checkout-service in production-us-east-2 is throwing 500 errors right
now. Investigate the root cause using app-269-prod-logs.

report.summary: Data for the cluster the question names does exist: the only reachable Elasticsearch index, app-269-prod-logs, holds 6 documents with date field `timestamp`, 4 tagged cluster=production-us-east-2 and 2 tagged production-eu-west-2. In production-us-east-2 the log evidence shows payment-service's charge call to the external provider stripe-us ending in an upstream timeout after 30000ms, checkout-service reporting a payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us), checkout-service then reporting 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)', and finally 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open' at 17:34:54Z — i.e. the 500s are the visible symptom of the payment path failing. The deepest failure the evidence names is the external provider stripe-us; no available source covers stripe-us itself or payment-service's own egress metrics, so whether the 30s delay originates at the provider or inside payment-service's client path is unverified. The 2 production-eu-west-2 records are a different cluster and are healthy INFO lines ('Healthy: p95 latency 220ms', 'Adyen-eu healthy'); they are not evidence of this incident and give no baseline. Kubernetes objects reachable in this Run belong to a separate single-node lab cluster (node opspilot-m1-control-plane, otel-demo Prometheus alert rule labelled cluster: opspilot-m1); its namespace app-269 Deployment checkout-service runs nginx:1.27-alpine, is 1/1 ready with a pod of 0 restarts whose logs contain only nginx startup notices, and was created at 18:04:52Z, after the us-east-2 errors — that lab workload is not the failing checkout-service. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable on every attempt, so there is no error-rate, latency or trace corroboration and no pre-incident baseline anywhere in the delivered data. Conclusion is partial: log evidence only, with the provider side and the production-us-east-2 workload objects unobservable.

claims.text: The only reachable Elasticsearch index is app-269-prod-logs (docs.count 6, health green), whose mapped fields are cluster, level, message, service, timestamp and whose date field is `timestamp` (a search without time_field failed with TIME_FIELD_REQUIRED).

Across the whole authorized window app-269-prod-logs matches exactly 6 documents: by cluster production-us-east-2=4 and production-eu-west-2=2; by level ERROR=4 and INFO=2; by service checkout-service=4 and payment-service=2.
checkout-service in cluster production-us-east-2 logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T16:04:54Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (stripe-us)'.
payment-service in cluster production-us-east-2 logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T16:04:54Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.

checkout-service in cluster production-us-east-2 logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T17:04:54Z 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41%)' and ERROR at 2026-11-23T17:34:54Z 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open'.

The two production-eu-west-2 records in the same index are level INFO, not errors: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 2026-11-23T16:04:54Z and payment-service 'Adyen-eu healthy' at 2026-11-23T17:34:54Z; they come from a different cluster and provide no comparable baseline for production-us-east-2.

The earliest document in app-269-prod-logs is 2026-11-23T16:04:54Z and the index contains only 6 documents, so the sampled data has no pre-incident error-rate or latency samples for production-us-east-2.

The only Deployment named checkout-service that Kubernetes access exposes is in namespace app-269 on node opspilot-m1-control-plane: image nginx:1.27-alpine, replicas 1, readyReplicas 1, Available=True, with last write by kubectl-client-side-apply at 2026-11-23T18:04:52Z; its pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-fptpk started 2026-11-23T18:04:52Z with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance.

The logs of pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-fptpk (namespace app-269) contain 23 lines, all nginx/docker-entrypoint startup notices between 2026-11-23T18:04:54Z and 18:04:55Z, with no application error, checkout or payment text.

Grouped events across all namespaces cover only namespace app-269 in the queried slice 2026-11-23T18:04:52Z–18:04:54Z: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet×1, Pod Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started×1 each, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate×1 — all normal lifecycle reasons, with no failure, eviction, OOM or probe-failure event.

The Kubernetes objects readable in this Run carry the identity of a separate lab cluster, not production-us-east-2: the single node is opspilot-m1-control-plane, pod inventory spans kube-system/local-path-storage/otel-demo/app-269 all on that node, and the otel-demo Prometheus alert rule labels its alerts cluster: opspilot-m1.

The only ConfigMap in namespace app-269 is kube-root-ca.crt (last write kube-controller-manager 2026-11-23T18:04:52Z); there is no application ConfigMap carrying checkout or payment settings in that namespace.

The only fault-injection settings found (ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo, lab cluster opspilot-m1, helm-applied 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z) show paymentFailure defaultVariant 'off' and paymentUnreachable defaultVariant 'off', and every other demo flag (cartFailure, adFailure, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) also has defaultVariant 'off', so no enabled injected payment fault is visible in the delivered config; this config describes the lab demo cluster, not production-us-east-2.

The checkout 500s trace to payment-service's charge call to the external provider stripe-us timing out after 30000ms at 16:04:54Z; the resulting failures drove payment-service's reported failure rate to 41%, which opened checkout-service's circuit breaker for payment-service by 17:04:54Z, after which /api/checkout failed with 'circuit-breaker open'. Whether the 30s delay originated at stripe-us or in payment-service's client/egress path is unresolved.

A second candidate that remains open is a fault inside payment-service itself (client timeout configuration, egress/network refusal, or resource pressure) producing the 30s upstream timeout; no metric, trace or pod-level evidence for the production-us-east-2 payment-service was available to confirm or exclude it.

Rejected: that the nginx checkout-service Deployment/pod in lab namespace app-269 explains the production-us-east-2 500s. It has readyReplicas 1, restartCount 0, no previous container, only clean nginx startup logs, and was created at 2026-11-23T18:04:52Z, after the last us-east-2 error at 17:34:54Z; it is also outside the production-us-east-2 cluster.

Advice: confirm the cause by checking stripe-us provider status/latency and payment-service's outbound charge latency and timeout configuration for production-us-east-2, then enable Prometheus (error-rate/latency for checkout /api/checkout and payment charge) and Jaeger traces for that cluster to verify the timeout-to-circuit-breaker chain and to obtain a pre-incident baseline before remediating.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on execute_prometheus_instant_query and get_metric_names), so no error-rate, latency or series data exists for the named cluster and tickle series such as traces_span_metrics_calls_total were never read; the error and latency signals beyond the log lines are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on traces_list_services, traces_search and traces_search_by_tags), so no span-level confirmation of the checkout→payment→stripe-us path exists and no call chain can be asserted.
No source in this Run covers the external payment provider stripe-us itself, so the provider-side 30s delay is unverified.

Kubernetes access exposes only a lab cluster whose data (node opspilot-m1-control-plane, alert rule label cluster: opspilot-m1, otel-demo demo workloads) carries no production-us-east-2 identity; the production-us-east-2 checkout-service and payment-service Deployment/Pod objects could not be read, so their replicas, restarts, events and container logs are unknown.

The query for Services in namespace app-269 returned nothing (0 objects); this only shows that query matched nothing and does not prove that no Service endpoints exist there, so service-to-endpoint wiring for the lab checkout-service remains unchecked.
The log index holds only 6 documents from 2026-11-23T16:04:54Z to 17:34:54Z; the exact start of the failure, its resolution, and any pre-incident baseline are unknown.
The change_history integration is not integrated, so whether a deployment, config or provider-side change preceded the 16:04:54Z timeout could not be checked.

Because the flagd-config fault settings are currently 'off' and the time they were last changed is not visible (only a helm Apply at 14:36:29Z), fault injection can be neither confirmed nor ruled out for the incident window, and it belongs to the lab cluster anyway.
next_steps: Check stripe-us provider status, latency and error rate for 2026-11-23T16:00Z onward and correlate with the 30s charges timeout.
Review payment-service charge client timeout/retry and egress configuration in production-us-east-2, and checkout-service circuit-breaker thresholds.
Enable Prometheus and Jaeger for production-us-east-2 and query checkout POST /api/checkout 5xx ratio and payment charge latency around 16:04:54Z–17:34:54Z to establish a baseline.
Enable the change_history integration to check whether a payment-service or provider configuration change preceded 16:04:54Z.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

data.prometheus.yml:
global:
  evaluation_interval: 1m
  scrape_interval: 1m
  scrape_timeout: 10s
storage:
  tsdb:
    out_of_order_time_window: 30m
otlp:
    keep_identifying_resource_attributes: true
    promote_resource_attributes:
    - opspilot.integration.id
    - service.instance.id
    - service.name
    - service.namespace
    - service.version
    - cloud.availability_zone
    - cloud.region
    - deployment.environment.name
    - k8s.cluster.name
    - k8s.container.name
    - k8s.cronjob.name
    - k8s.daemonset.name
    - k8s.deployment.name
    - k8s.job.name
    - k8s.namespace.name
    - k8s.node.name
    - k8s.pod.name
    - k8s.replicaset.name
    - k8s.statefulset.name
    - container.name
    - host.name
rule_files:
- /etc/config/recording_rules.yml
- /etc/config/alerting_rules.yml
- /etc/config/rules
- /etc/config/alerts
scrape_configs:
- job_name: prometheus
  static_configs:
  - targets:
    - localhost:9090
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-apiservers
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: endpoints
  relabel_configs:
  - action: keep
    regex: default;kubernetes;https
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_namespace
    - __meta_kubernetes_service_name
    - __meta_kubernetes_endpoint_port_name
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-nodes
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: node
  relabel_configs:
  - action: labelmap
    regex: __meta_kubernetes_node_label_(.+)
  - replacement: kubernetes.default.svc:443
    target_label: __address__
  - regex: (.+)
    replacement: /api/v1/nodes/$1/proxy/metrics
    source_labels:
    - __meta_kubernetes_node_name
    target_label: __metrics_path__
  scheme: https
  tls_config:
    ca_file: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt
- bearer_token_file: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
  job_name: kubernetes-nodes-cadvisor
  kubernetes_sd_configs:
  - role: node

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
